title: Patch-pocket requests & annotary (week-of 2026-11-03)
content:
Purpose: quick, customer-driven catalog of small fixes and low-risk feature patches that unblock production pain. Not a roadmap commit — a living stash for micro-deploys and canary probes.

Topline threads (short):
- Major: enterprise client A reporting token-surge + KV cache eviction at 4k seq -> frequent cold-starts and token spikes (repro steps below). Asks: better cache pre-warm or sticky-session routing to Dedicated pools. Jira: CS-4827.
- Minor: multiple teams asking for per-request cost breakdown in Console when using model variants (they want token-level attribution + per-model slot).
- UX nudge: clearer error proto when function-calls fail due to schema mismatch — customers patch by re-sending entire convo; need structured error with suggested corrective action.

Customer quotes (unedited):
- "We keep seeing costs spike midday and it’s always a few API calls with massive context. Hard to trace." — eng lead, fintech customer
- "When we fall back from quantized model to fp16, latency halved but quality regressed. We need automatic scorecard for output delta before rollouts." — ML platform PM

Requests & suggested band-aids (priority / reproducibility / engineering note):
1) KV-cache pre-warm toggle (P1 / reproducible / small feature): add customer-configurable TTL and a pre-warm API for pinned prefixes. Implementation: add API endpoint to push prefixes into cache + admin console toggle. Expected effort: small backend + UI flag. Quick test: Dedicated pool A/B.
2) Per-call token attribution (P1 / intermittent / backend+console): surface model variant, token count, and per-token cost in request logs and Console row. Short-term: add columns in DB export. Long-term: realtime UI.
3) Structured function-call error body (P2 / reproducible / runtime): include a "suggested_fix" field with sample corrected schema and example call. Low-risk change in runtime error layer.
4) Auto-rollback thresholds for quality regressions (P2 / hard-to-reproduce / product+applied-ml): define a lightweight eval harness for canary traffic — compute BLEU/embedding drift and trigger automatic rollback if delta > threshold. Start as opt-in.
5) Dedicated burst policy clarity (P3 / reproducible / docs + console): customers confused about burst throttles vs autoscale. Action: docs snippet + Console banner + sample config.

Repro steps for KV cache cold-start (customer A):
1. Send a 6k-token prompt with small repeated prefix X from 100 unique sessions within 2m.
2. Observe KV cache misses and sudden token/sec increase.
3. If routed across two different Dedicated pools, see TTL mismatch.
Notes: appears sensitive to session affinity; routing TTL shorter than model KV lifetime.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Should pre-warm be per-customer (Tenant-scoped) or per-route? (ops scaling trade-offs)
- Risk appetite: allow pre-warm in Private deployments where customer controls keys? (security concerns)
- Can we prototype structured errors behind a feature flag to collect usage without affecting GA errors?

Action items (short):
- CS: Rally customer A for sample traces and set up canary with dev-serving team (owner: Marcus). Due: 2026-11-10.
- Eng/runtime: quick spike assessment for sticky routing TTL mismatch (owner: Ravi). Due: 2026-11-12.
- Product: draft spec for per-call attribution columns for export (owner: Eileen). Due: 2026-11-17.
- PM/Applied-ML: sketch eval harness for canary rollouts (owner: Sofia). Due: 2026-11-21.

Notes to self / loose thinking:
- Could implement a low-cost heuristic: when a request size > 3k tokens, always route to a warmed pool to reduce cold penalty. Might be acceptable as interim.
- For Private, pre-warm API could be combined with KMS audit logs to record pre-warm actions (auditability ask).

Quick links / evidence snippets:
- Slack thread: #cs-kv-cache-> https://slack.redwood.ai/archives/C0ABC1234/p1698800000000
- Sample trace (anonymized) attached in Jira CS-4827 (see attachments)

Status: collecting traces and alignment with runtime. This doc meant to be a compact, actionable slice — use for sprint planning and patch-proposal PRs.

-- end of patch-pocket annotary --
